items.statement: Ensure laboratory records include complete data from every test needed to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays, covering the record elements listed below.
items.quote: Laboratory records shall include complete data derived from all tests necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays, as follows:

items.statement: Laboratory records must include complete data from all tests needed to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays, including a description of the sample received for testing: its source (the location where it was obtained), quantity, lot number or other distinctive code, date sampled and date received for testing.
items.quote: A description of the sample received for testing with identification of source (that is, location from where sample was obtained), quantity, lot number or other distinctive code, date sample was taken, and date sample was received for testing.

items.statement: Laboratory records must include complete data from all tests needed to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays, including a statement of each method used to test the sample.
items.quote: A statement of each method used in the testing of the sample.

items.statement: Laboratory records must include complete data from all tests needed to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays: the method statement must point to where the data are kept showing the methods meet proper standards of accuracy and reliability for the product tested; if the method is in the current USP, National Formulary, AOAC INTERNATIONAL Book of Methods or another recognized standard reference, or is detailed in an approved new drug application, and is used unmodified, stating the method and its reference is sufficient.
items.quote: The statement shall indicate the location of data that establish that the methods used in the testing of the sample meet proper standards of accuracy and reliability as applied to the product tested. (If the method employed is in the current revision of the United States Pharmacopeia, National Formulary, AOAC INTERNATIONAL, Book of Methods, 1 or in other recognized standard references, or is detailed in an approved new drug application and the referenced method is not modified, a statement indicating the method and reference will suffice).

items.statement: Verify the suitability of every testing method used under actual conditions of use, and document this in the laboratory records.
items.quote: The suitability of all testing methods used shall be verified under actual conditions of use.

items.statement: Laboratory records must include complete data from all tests needed to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays, including a statement of the weight or measure of sample used for each test, where appropriate.
items.quote: A statement of the weight or measure of sample used for each test, where appropriate.

items.statement: Laboratory records must include complete data from all tests needed to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays, including a complete record of all data obtained during each test, including all instrument graphs, charts and spectra, properly identified to show the specific component, container, closure, in-process material or drug product and lot tested.
items.quote: A complete record of all data secured in the course of each test, including all graphs, charts, and spectra from laboratory instrumentation, properly identified to show the specific component, drug product container, closure, in-process material, or drug product, and lot tested.

items.statement: Laboratory records must include complete data from all tests needed to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays, including a record of all calculations made for the test, including units of measure, conversion factors and equivalency factors.
items.quote: A record of all calculations performed in connection with the test, including units of measure, conversion factors, and equivalency factors.

items.statement: Laboratory records must include complete data from all tests needed to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays, including a statement of the test results and how they compare with established standards of identity, strength, quality and purity for the component, container, closure, in-process material or drug product tested.
items.quote: A statement of the results of tests and how the results compare with established standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity for the component, drug product container, closure, in-process material, or drug product tested.

items.statement: Laboratory records must include complete data from all tests needed to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays, including the initials or signature of the person performing each test and the date or dates the tests were performed.
items.quote: The initials or signature of the person who performs each test and the date(s) the tests were performed.

items.statement: Laboratory records must include complete data from all tests needed to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays, including the initials or signature of a second person showing the original records were reviewed for accuracy, completeness and compliance with established standards.
items.quote: The initials or signature of a second person showing that the original records have been reviewed for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with established standards.

items.statement: Maintain complete records of any modification to an established test method.
items.quote: Complete records shall be maintained of any modification of an established method employed in testing.
items.condition: when an established method is modified

items.statement: Ensure records of a test method modification include the reason for it and data verifying that the modified method gives results at least as accurate and reliable for the material tested as the established method.
items.quote: Such records shall include the reason for the modification and data to verify that the modification produced results that are at least as accurate and reliable for the material being tested as the established method.
items.condition: when an established method is modified

items.statement: Maintain complete records of all testing and standardization of laboratory reference standards, reagents and standard solutions.
items.quote: Complete records shall be maintained of any testing and standardization of laboratory reference standards, reagents, and standard solutions.

items.statement: Maintain complete records of the required periodic calibration of laboratory instruments, apparatus, gauges and recording devices.
items.quote: Complete records shall be maintained of the periodic calibration of laboratory instruments, apparatus, gauges, and recording devices required by § 211.160(b)(4).

items.statement: Maintain complete records of all stability testing performed under the written stability testing program.
items.quote: Complete records shall be maintained of all stability testing performed in accordance with § 211.166.

items.statement: Ensure distribution records contain the product name and strength, a description of the dosage form, the consignee's name and address, the date and quantity shipped, and the lot or control number of the drug product.
items.quote: Distribution records shall contain the name and strength of the product and description of the dosage form, name and address of the consignee, date and quantity shipped, and lot or control number of the drug product.

items.statement: Establish and follow written procedures for handling all written and oral complaints about a drug product.
items.quote: Written procedures describing the handling of all written and oral complaints regarding a drug product shall be established and followed.

items.statement: Ensure complaint procedures provide for quality control unit review of any complaint involving a possible failure of a drug product to meet any of its specifications and, for such products, a decision on whether a failure investigation is needed.
items.quote: Such procedures shall include provisions for review by the quality control unit, of any complaint involving the possible failure of a drug product to meet any of its specifications and, for such drug products, a determination as to the need for an investigation in accordance with § 211.192.

items.statement: Ensure complaint procedures provide for review of whether a complaint represents a serious and unexpected adverse drug experience that must be reported to FDA.
items.quote: Such procedures shall include provisions for review to determine whether the complaint represents a serious and unexpected adverse drug experience which is required to be reported to the Food and Drug Administration in accordance with §§ 310.305 and 514.80 of this chapter.

items.statement: Maintain a written record of each complaint in a file designated for drug product complaints.
items.quote: A written record of each complaint shall be maintained in a file designated for drug product complaints.

items.statement: Keep the drug product complaint file at the establishment where the product was manufactured, processed or packed, or at another facility provided the written records are readily available for inspection there.
items.quote: The file regarding such drug product complaints shall be maintained at the establishment where the drug product involved was manufactured, processed, or packed, or such file may be maintained at another facility if the written records in such files are readily available for inspection at that other facility.
items.condition: other facility only if records readily available for inspection

items.statement: Retain written complaint records for a drug product until at least 1 year after the product's expiration date or 1 year after the complaint was received, whichever is longer.
items.quote: Written records involving a drug product shall be maintained until at least 1 year after the expiration date of the drug product, or 1 year after the date that the complaint was received, whichever is longer.

items.statement: For OTC drug products without expiration dating because they meet the exemption criteria, retain written complaint records for 3 years after distribution of the product.
items.quote: In the case of certain OTC drug products lacking expiration dating because they meet the criteria for exemption under § 211.137, such written records shall be maintained for 3 years after distribution of the drug product.
items.condition: OTC product exempt from expiration dating

items.statement: Ensure each written complaint record includes, where known, the drug product name and strength, lot number, complainant's name, nature of the complaint and the reply to the complainant.
items.quote: The written record shall include the following information, where known: the name and strength of the drug product, lot number, name of complainant, nature of complaint, and reply to complainant.

items.statement: Where a failure investigation of a complaint is conducted, include the investigation findings and follow-up in the written complaint record.
items.quote: Where an investigation under § 211.192 is conducted, the written record shall include the findings of the investigation and followup.

items.statement: Where a failure investigation of a complaint is conducted, keep the investigation record or a copy of it at the establishment where the investigation took place, in line with record retention requirements.
items.quote: The record or copy of the record of the investigation shall be maintained at the establishment where the investigation occurred in accordance with § 211.180(c).

items.statement: Where no failure investigation of a complaint is conducted, include in the written complaint record the reason an investigation was judged unnecessary and the name of the responsible person who decided this.
items.quote: Where an investigation under § 211.192 is not conducted, the written record shall include the reason that an investigation was found not to be necessary and the name of the responsible person making such a determination.

items.statement: Identify returned drug products as returned and hold them.
items.quote: Returned drug products shall be identified as such and held.

items.statement: Destroy a returned drug product if the conditions under which it was held, stored or shipped before or during return, or the condition of the product, its container, carton or labeling as a result of storage or shipping, cast doubt on its safety, identity, strength, quality or purity, unless examination, testing or other investigation proves it meets appropriate standards of safety, identity, strength, quality or purity.
items.quote: If the conditions under which returned drug products have been held, stored, or shipped before or during their return, or if the condition of the drug product, its container, carton, or labeling, as a result of storage or shipping, casts doubt on the safety, identity, strength, quality or purity of the drug product, the returned drug product shall be destroyed unless examination, testing, or other investigations prove the drug product meets appropriate standards of safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity.
items.condition: if conditions cast doubt, unless proven to meet standards

items.statement: A returned drug product may be reprocessed, provided the resulting drug product meets appropriate standards, specifications and characteristics.
items.quote: A drug product may be reprocessed provided the subsequent drug product meets appropriate standards, specifications, and characteristics.

items.statement: Maintain records of returned drug products that include the name and label potency of the dosage form, lot, control or batch number, reason for return, quantity returned, date of disposition and ultimate disposition.
items.quote: Records of returned drug products shall be maintained and shall include the name and label potency of the drug product dosage form, lot number (or control number or batch number), reason for the return, quantity returned, date of disposition, and ultimate disposition of the returned drug product.

items.statement: If the reason for a return implicates associated batches, conduct an appropriate failure investigation that meets the batch investigation requirements.
items.quote: If the reason for a drug product being returned implicates associated batches, an appropriate investigation shall be conducted in accordance with the requirements of § 211.192.
items.condition: if return reason implicates associated batches

items.statement: Have written procedures for holding, testing and reprocessing returned drug products, and follow them.
items.quote: Procedures for the holding, testing, and reprocessing of returned drug products shall be in writing and shall be followed.

items.statement: Do not salvage and return to the market drug products that were subjected to improper storage conditions, including extremes of temperature, humidity, smoke, fumes, pressure, age or radiation, caused by natural disasters, fires, accidents or equipment failures.
items.quote: Drug products that have been subjected to improper storage conditions including extremes in temperature, humidity, smoke, fumes, pressure, age, or radiation due to natural disasters, fires, accidents, or equipment failures shall not be salvaged and returned to the marketplace.

items.statement: Where it is in question whether drug products were subjected to such improper storage conditions, conduct salvaging only if there is both evidence from laboratory tests and assays (including animal feeding studies where applicable) that the products meet all applicable standards of identity, strength, quality and purity, and evidence from inspection of the premises that the products and their packaging were not subjected to improper storage conditions from the disaster or accident.
items.quote: Whenever there is a question whether drug products have been subjected to such conditions, salvaging operations may be conducted only if there is (a) evidence from laboratory tests and assays (including animal feeding studies where applicable) that the drug products meet all applicable standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity and (b) evidence from inspection of the premises that the drug products and their associated packaging were not subjected to improper storage conditions as a result of the disaster or accident.
items.condition: whenever exposure to improper conditions is in question

items.statement: Accept organoleptic examinations only as supplemental evidence that salvaged drug products meet appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.
items.quote: Organoleptic examinations shall be acceptable only as supplemental evidence that the drug products meet appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity.

items.statement: Maintain records, including name, lot number and disposition, for drug products subject to salvaging requirements.
items.quote: Records including name, lot number, and disposition shall be maintained for drug products subject to this section.
